hook: Heads, you win $150. Tails, you lose $100. Do you flip?
open_loop: Line 3 plants two promises: 'the math says yes' and 'why does your brain refuse?'. The brain half (the ~2x number) is withheld until line 6 (~60% in); the math half (+$25 per flip, <2% chance of ending behind over 100 flips) is withheld until the last ~8 s (lines 9-10).
payoff: Your brain weighs a loss about twice as heavily as a win (meta-analysis mean 1.955), so the $100 loss feels like about $195 and beats the $150 win. Twist: on average each flip pays +$25, and over 100 flips you end up behind less than 2% of the time.

lines.text: Heads, you win $150. Tails, you lose $100. Do you flip?
lines.say: Heads, you win a hundred fifty dollars. Tails, you lose a hundred dollars. Do you flip?
lines.ph: Heads, panalo ka ng $150. Tails, talo ka ng $100. I-flip mo ba?
lines.visual: Frame 0: Psychology Benny already holding a giant gold coin up to camera, one brow up (hmm). Green '+$150' pops on the left, red '-$100' on the right. No title card; first word at 0.0 s.
Quick cut: a crowd of tiny stick figures all shaking heads; a big red 'NO' stamp slams down. Benny shrugs (pose shrug, expression thinking).

lines.text: But the *math* says yes. So why does your brain refuse?
lines.ph: Pero sabi ng *math*, oo. E bakit ayaw ng utak mo?
lines.visual: Split screen: a calculator with a green check vs. Benny's pink brain with a red X. Benny points at the brain (pose point, expression thinking). A '?' pulses over the brain.
Rubber stamp 'LOSS AVERSION' thuds across the screen; Benny pushes up his round glasses (pose present, expression smug).

lines.say: Researchers pooled six hundred seven measurements from a hundred fifty papers.
lines.ph: Pinagsama ng researchers ang 607 measurements mula sa 150 papers.
lines.visual: Paper stacks fly in and pile up beside Benny; a counter races up to 607. Benny scrolls through them (pose scroll, expression thinking).

lines.text: The verdict: losing hurts about *twice* as much as winning feels good.
lines.ph: Ang resulta: mas masakit ang talo, mga *doble*, kaysa sa saya ng panalo.
lines.visual: Zoom punch on Benny, eyes wide (expression shocked, pose shock). A giant '~2x' slams in; a scale tips hard toward a red 'LOSS' weight.

lines.text: So that $100 loss feels like about $195.
lines.say: So that hundred-dollar loss feels like about a hundred ninety-five dollars.
lines.ph: Kaya 'yung $100 na talo, parang mga $195 ang sakit.
lines.visual: Benny holds the pink brain; the red '-$100' bar stretches upward and relabels to 'feels like -$195'. Benny winces (expression broke, pose worry).

lines.text: *Bigger* than your $150 win. So you say no.
lines.say: Bigger than your hundred-fifty-dollar win. So you say no.
lines.ph: *Mas malaki* pa sa $150 na panalo mo. Kaya ayaw mo.
lines.visual: Two bars side by side: red 'feels -$195' towers over green 'real +$150'. Benny slumps and pockets the coin (pose slump).

lines.text: But on average, each flip *pays you* $25.
lines.say: But on average, each flip pays you twenty-five dollars.
lines.ph: Pero sa average, bawat flip, *kumikita ka* ng $25.
lines.visual: Benny pulls the coin back out with a smug 'alam ko na' half-lidded grin (expression smug, pose flex). A green '+$25' counter ticks up over a fast coin-flip montage.

lines.text: Flip 100 times, and you end up behind less than 2% of the time.
lines.say: Flip a hundred times, and you end up behind less than two percent of the time.
lines.ph: Mag-flip ka ng 100 beses, talo ka sa dulo wala pang 2% ng chance.
lines.visual: A '100 FLIPS' counter spins to 100; a mini pie chart shows a tiny red sliver labeled '<2%'. Benny's jaw drops then grins (expression shocked to happy, pose present).

lines.text: One flip is still 50/50. So how much would *you* need to win? Comment it.
lines.say: One flip is still fifty-fifty. So how much would you need to win? Comment it.
lines.ph: Isang flip, 50/50 pa rin. So magkano ang kailangan mong panalo? I-comment mo.
lines.visual: Benny holds the coin up to camera exactly like frame 0 (seamless loop), gap-tooth grin (expression happy, pose point at viewer). Small corner tag 'Not financial advice' stays on screen through this scene. Hard cut on the last word.

disclaimer_on_screen: Not financial advice (corner tag, final scene; brain/decision thought experiment, not advice to gamble)

facts_used.claim: In the coin toss (win $150 / lose $100), most people decline.
Most people reject a 50/50 win $150 / lose $100 flip even though it is positive on average (corroborating).
Meta-analysis of 607 loss-aversion estimates from 150 articles; mean coefficient 1.955 (losses weigh about 2x an equal gain).
Losses tend to be treated as about twice as large as an equivalent gain; named 'loss aversion'.
The ~2:1 ratio varies by context (hence 'about twice', not 'exactly').
+$25 average per flip; $100 loss 'feels like' about $195 at weight 1.955.
Chance of ending behind after 100 fair flips = 1.76% (<2%); a single flip is 50/50.

math_check: Average per flip = 0.5*150 - 0.5*100 = +$25. Felt loss = 1.955*100 = $195.50 -> said as 'about $195' (range 182.00-210.20, all > $150). Felt value = 75 - 97.75 = -$22.75. 100 flips with h heads: total = 150h - 100(100-h) = 250h - 10,000 < 0 iff h < 40; P(h <= 39 | n=100, p=0.5) = 0.017600 = 1.76% < 2%. Expected total over 100 flips = 100*25 = +$2,500 (not stated in script). Re-computed in .venv python.
